Scope: skills/objectstack-data/rules/field-types.md, skills/objectstack-data/rules/relationships.md, skills/objectstack-ui/rules/dashboards.md + none

The diff is four files: the three `hits` and one changeset. No file in it implements or enforces the taught rules; the lint, its `os explain` text and the CLI were read on the PR base `4bba8b8f02f`, not reviewed. The changeset is the lane seat's ACCEPT.

### ① Derived judgments

- Accept set: unchanged. No schema, lint, runtime or CLI file is in the diff; nothing an author can write is newly accepted or refused. Right.
- Public surface: the published skill text of `@objectstack/skills` changes in three rule files. One owner sentence (relationships.md, Computed column) and two pointers; no SKILL.md, no eval, no reference index touched. Right.
- Severity taught: `warning` at both rule ids, never a refusal. Agrees with `packages/lint/src/stored-expression-inputs.ts` (both issues `severity: 'warning'`) and with the card pointer 6837754404. Right.
- Token ceilings: no ceiling file is in the diff, so none moved. `Lint · docs & code guards`, `Lint · repo & tooling gates`, `Lint · ESLint`, `Check Changeset`, `Check PR Size`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `PR-body guards`, `Build Core`, `Type Check · source gates`, `Type Check · workspace` and `Lint · CI, release & engine gates` concluded success on this head.
- Still in progress when this record was written, so not yet verdicts: `Test Core (1/8)`, `Test Core (2/8)`, `Type Check · consumer gates`. The seat reads them before it adopts this record; a text-only diff gives none of them a path to judge, but their conclusions are theirs.

### ② Semver level

`'@objectstack/skills': patch` matches what the diff publishes: teaching text for behaviour that already shipped, no new capability and nothing withdrawn. The package name resolves (`packages/skills/package.json`).

Clause-②: no. Holds: the diff changes no accept set and no served shape. `Metadata-protocol: none` holds for the same reason.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: empty. Nothing to answer.
- Deviation, one owner sentence plus two pointers instead of three full sentences: accepted. The card asks for the content in each place; a pointer to one owner delivers it and the lane does not duplicate rules.
- Deviation, the dashboards existing-rows clause rewritten: judged in ④, holds.
- Deviation, token payment by deleting restating comments and asides: judged in ④, no rule lost.
- Deviation, no eval added: accepted, the order lists it as optional. The card has no eval prompt, so ④ judges the text against the card's ask and the code on `main`.
- Deviations on the PR trailer and commit trailer are process, not contract; not judged here.
- No escalation.

### ④ Design judgment

**skills/objectstack-data/rules/relationships.md** (the owner sentence). Read against `stored-expression-inputs.ts`, `rule-explanations.ts` (both explanations) and `packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/stored-expressions.ts` with `packages/objectql/src/stored-expression-backfill.ts`.

- Holds: "keeps what it held at this row's last write" is the lint's own consequence. `record.product.unit_price` is a counted read (one hop through a `lookup` the example declares, not the hop's `id`). The two forward routes, a `formula` (read time, not totallable) and a snapshot a flow on the related object writes, are the finding's first two ways forward, in its words. The command line is the finding's third, flag for flag: `--field` depends on `--object`, `--changed` recomputes differing values, `--apply` writes. `now()`, `today()`, the acting user and `can()` are all counted volatile inputs and "fixed at the write" is the finding's consequence.
- Tried to break it: "It reads only that row" is a rule for the author, not the engine's behaviour (the engine does read one hop, which is why the warning exists); the next clause says what happens when the rule is broken, so the sentence does not mislead. The bullet's standing advice "keep it stored so the parent `summary` can roll it up" does not collide: the example's `amount` reads `record.unit_price`, the line's own column, which Catalog auto-fill copies from the product.
- **should-fix (S1).** "...or is a snapshot a flow on the related object writes; repair drift with `os migrate stored-expressions --object OBJECT --field FIELD --changed --apply`." The nearest reading is that the command repairs the snapshot's drift. It does not: a flow-written snapshot declares no `expression`, and the backfill refuses a `--field` that "is not a stored computed field" before it reads a row. The command repairs one thing only, a stored expression that already reads a related record and was kept, which is the lint's separate third way forward. The sentence has just told the agent not to keep that shape, so the repair clause has no subject. Name the subject, for example "a field left stored: repair its drift with ...". Five tokens of headroom remain in the file; the fix fits or pays in-file.
- nit (N1). The volatile list is a subset: `daysFromNow()`, `daysAgo()` and `hasCapability()` are counted too. The sentence does not claim to be complete and it is the card's own list; the finding names the exact spelling when it fires.
- nit (N2). No remedy is given for a volatile input (the finding says: a `formula` to show the current value, a scheduled flow to keep a stored one current). The card did not ask for it.
- Cuts: the six example comments, the `relatedListTitle` comment, "(the same source the lookup picker uses)", "(ADR-0085)" and the many-to-many comment. Each fact still stands in the file or its named home: the Sort field, Catalog auto-fill and Computed column bullets; the `relatedListTitle` sentence; `objectstack-data/SKILL.md` line 97 for the lookup picker; the heading and the remaining comment for many-to-many. "typeahead" now lives only in `objectstack-ui/SKILL.md`, which is the section this one already defers to. No rule lost.

**skills/objectstack-data/rules/field-types.md.** The `formula` row's added "that reads only its own row (relationships.md → Computed column)" is a pointer to the owner and says nothing the owner does not. It holds. The cut "Source of truth: ...field.zod.ts" has its home at `skills/objectstack-data/references/_index.md` line 13. No rule lost.

**skills/objectstack-ui/rules/dashboards.md.**

- "existing rows: `os migrate stored-expressions --apply`" is true of `main`: the command exists, its default run (no `--changed`) fills exactly the rows that hold a NULL the expression gives a value, and `--apply` is what writes. It is also the remedy `rule-explanations.ts` gives for this very pair ("until each is written again or `os migrate stored-expressions --apply` fills them"). The dropped "no hosted backfill yet" was stale and is a separate concern the new text does not claim: a save in publish mode or a publish now fills at the change (`protocol-stored-expression-fill.ts`, `content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx`), and the command is for a definition changed in a repository and booted.
- The phrase "computed and stored on write" that `VIRTUAL_FIELD_AGGREGATE_REMEDY` carries is kept. The `days_count` example reads the row's own `date` fields, so it agrees with "from its own row only".
- nit (N3). The clause no longer says the existing rows are empty until filled, so a total reads low; the command's presence implies it. And the command needs the database URL, while a publish-mode save needs nothing; neither is said. Follow-up material, not a defect.
- Cuts: four ADR-0021 asides. Citations, not rules; the heading "Server-side date bucketing ... (ADR-0021)" and the example comment still carry the ADR. No eval `expected_output` names a deleted fact.

Findings: S1 should-fix; N1, N2, N3 nits. No must-fix. S1's fix moves the head and earns a delta review of the Computed column sentence.
